entry.title: How to heal and restore health in Slay the Spire 2
entry.summary:
Slay the Spire 2 isn't your typical deckbuilder, where you don't have to take care of your health.
While there are five different characters to pick from, none of them is immortal. They will all take damage, and they will perish if you're not careful. Taking damage is inevitable; no matter what you do, you'll always end up receiving damage.
What matters is whether you're healing your character at the correct moments.
How to heal in Slay the Spire 2
Healing is a premium activity in Slay the Spire 2. You can't heal whenever you want, and restoring HP comes at a price. You'll occasionally come across Rest Spots that appear as a campfire on your path. These spots can be found only sporadically, so you'll need to plan carefully. Their locations on every run is compeltely random.
Screenshot by Destructoid
When you're at the spot, you'll have two different options: Rest or Smith. If you choose the latter, you can improve a card by applying different upgrades. If you choose the former, you'll be able to recover a percentage of your character's lost health.
You can also find different Relics and consumables on your run, and some of them might allow you to restore HP. Potions are one-time use, and you can have a maximum of three at a time. This method isn't a guaranteed solution since all runs are random. It could happen that you might be unable to find an applicable Relic or consumable.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Slay the Spire 2 has five characters, and one of them has a healing ability. The Ironclad's default relic, the Burning Blood, allows you to recover 6 HP at the end of combat. This is an extremely useful relic to have, which ranks him well on our characters' tier list.
Outside of these methods, there's no other way to recover HP and restore the health of your character in Slay the Spire 2. The same methods also apply if you're playing co-op with your friends.

entry.title: What are Schemas in Marathon?
entry.summary:
Marathon is a sensory overload when it comes to items being added and subtracted from your inventory, similar to other extraction shooters.
There is A LOT of different items to sift through, and while some are somewhat useless, many can help you out if you can figure out just what the heck they're for. Like Schemas. Found within the season one Rewards Pass, these items offer access to items for you to buy using Credits so that you will always have a Loadout ready to go (and instantly lose) when you play a round.
Here's everything there is to know about Schemas in Marathon and what they do.
What is a Schema in Marathon?
Screenshot by Destructoid
In Marathon, a Schema is a voucher that will allow you to purchase specific weapons or items from the Armory at any time, meaning you don't have to worry about it being out of stock or on a timer, or available from a specific Faction.
Schemas are found multiple times within the season one Rewards Pass, and they must be unlocked with SILK, which is the free currency that you get by playing the game, extracting successfully, and completing objectives.
When you open the Armory screen, your owned Schemas can be found on the right side of the screen (illustrated in the image below). These items are still pretty pricy, so there's no discount, but the Schema makes sure that you can purchase it whenever you want, regardless of your ranking with each individual Faction.
Screenshot by Destructoid
A Schema voucher in the Rewards Pass gives you the ability to purchase that gun, no questions asked, up to three times apiece. As of now, it's not clear if these items last forever, but it's likely that they will also disappear with the rest of your loot during seasonal wipes when player inventories are reset.

entry.title: How to get more packs in Wikigacha
entry.summary:
Wikigacha has turned Wikipedia into a card-collecting game, and at its core lies the packs.
Just like any good TCG and CCG, you can open packs to increase your collection. As you might have imagined, Wikigacha has one of the largest card collections I have ever seen in a video game. Every Wikipedia page is a card for you to collect.
Let's find out how you can get more packs.
Best way to open more packs in Wikigacha
Unlike microtransaction-infested games of today, Wikigacha is completely free. Every pack you open can be earned without spending and there's no way for you to spend any money to get extra packs.
Screenshot by Destructoid
This is how the pack system works inside the game.
At any given time, you can hold at most 10 packs.
Once the number of packs in your collection goes down below 10, a timer will start. You'll gain a pack every minute for free. You'll get your pack even if you close the game.
However, you can have at most 10 packs by this method. Once you've received the 10th pack, the timer will stop. It will resume when you open at least one of your packs.
If you want to min-max your collection, you'll need to log in to the game every eight minutes or so and open as many packs as you can. If you open all the packs, you'll have 10 minutes before your storage is full.
There are additional ways to get more packs daily. The ones you earn from the daily tasks can bypass the 10-pack limit.
Open five packs
Pull at least one SR+ card
Open Wikipedia once
Share your result
Watch one ad
You'll get two extra packs for every task that you complete. If you complete all the tasks, you'll receive ten additional packs. Hence, you'll rarely run out of packs to open in Wikigacha, and the best part is that you don't have to spend a dime.
While you get to open many packs, you'll also need to get plenty of cards to complete your collection and build competitive decks.

entry.title: Slay the Spire 2’s explosive early access launch makes it the most-played roguelike in Steam’s history on day one
entry.summary:
Who's up slaying their spire? Well, a whole heck of a lot of gamers, that's who.
Slay the Spire 2's early access launch yesterday can only be described as a tremendous success. The long-anticipated sequel to one of the earliest and most popular roguelikes on Steam had such high demand that it caused issues on the app's store yesterday.
Image via MegaCrit
But eventually, error codes subsides, and the numbers started pouring in. Less than a day later, it sits at Overwhelmingly Positive with almost 5,000 reviews, and a shocking all-time peak (reached within the past hour as of publishing) of over 430,000 concurrent players. That's enough to instantly make it the most-played Steam game with the "roguelike" tag, ever.
On day one, it skyrocketed past Elden Ring Nightreign's previous record of 313,593, and utterly dwarfing the high of the original Slay the Spire's peak of 57,025. And the rest of the list is also nothing to scoff at: Hades 2, Megabonk, Vampire Survivors, Risk of Rain 2, and on and on.
Slay the Spire 2 adds on to the original game's formula with new characters and cards, but also online co-op, giving every card battler fan a reason to gift their friends the game (or bug them until they buy it), marking uncharted territory for the series.
These kinds of numbers are a dream for any game dev, let alone an indie team like MegaCrit, who have taken years to work on and iterate the sequel. It's a feel-good story for sure, especially when those are in short supply these days. I'm hoping to see some sales numbers soon, but either way, that many players on an indie roguelike card battler is impressive no matter how you look at it.

entry.title: How to play Slay the Spire 2 co-op with friends
entry.summary:
One of the biggest additions to Slay the Spire 2 is optional co-op. Unlike the first game, you choose to have a shared adventure with your friends.
Already added to the game at its early access launch, allows you to play with up to three friends and have a shared journey. If you've been confused about how to play co-op, this guide will help you out./yoast
Table of contents How to co-op with friends in Slay the Spire 2 Does Slay the Spire 2 have matchmaking
How to co-op with friends in Slay the Spire 2
For starters, you and your buddies will need to own Slay the Spire 2 since there's no system of friends pass or anything similar. All of you must be added to Steam as friends. To play co-op, you'll need to invite your friends.
Load the game.
From the main menu, choose multiplayer.
You have two options: you can either host a game or join one that's hosted by your buddy.
Let's assume you want to host a game.
Select the type of game you want to host.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Next, pick the save file to create the session. You can use one that you used to play solo, or create a new save. In-game progression, like unlocked characters, doesn't carry across different saves.
Now, you have to invite your friends from the Steam list.
Once your friend accepts your request, they will join your shared session. For co-op, the host must stay connected to the game at all times.
Does Slay the Spire 2 have matchmaking
While Slay the Spire 2 has co-op, there's no matchmaking. You can't host open sessions and play with strangers. However, you can add them as a friend on Steam and then send them the invite. This is a smart way to play with others if none of your friends are on Slay the Spire 2.

entry.title: USN-8075-1: GIMP vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
Michael Randrianantenaina discovered that calculating the linear size of a DDS file could overflow on 32-bit systems. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. This issue only affected Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-2760)
Michael Randrianantenaina discovered that GIMP did not perform any bounds checking when calculating an offset into XWD Colormaps. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2025-10934)
It was discovered that GIMP's PNM loader did not sufficiently check that the image could fit within the allocated memory, which could cause GIMP to read or write out-of-bounds. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2025-14422)
It was discovered that maliciously-crafted TGA files could cause memory corruption and leave GIMP in an inconsistent state. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2025-48797)
It was discovered that a maliciously-crafted XCF file could cause GIMP to free the same memory region twice, or access an already freed address. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2025-48798)

entry.title: USN-8073-1: QEMU vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
It was discovered that the UHCI controller implementation of QEMU could be brought into an invalid state. An attacker inside the guest could possibly use this issue to cause QEMU to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2024-8354)

entry.title: How Steven Spielberg, a Pinhead bust, and Robert De Niro's sex appeal gave us the horror shooter Clive Barker's Undying
entry.summary: "As a kid, I’d sometimes go to work with my dad," Brady Bell tells me. "We’d drive onto the MGM lot, and I’d see coin-op games through the window of one office. 'That’s Mr Spielberg’s office,' my dad would say. I remember thinking, 'Wow - he gets to make movies and play games. That’s the life." Years later, Bell found himself sitting in an LA office while the legendary director gave him notes. Modelers around them were working on outrageously expensive workstations, painstakingly creating mockups for Jurassic Park sequels. But there were no dinosaurs on Bell's screen, not even a tiny Compsognathus or a dinky little Anchiornis. Bell was showing Spielberg a cutscene packed with hellish creatures, occultish symbols, and the tastefully wood-panelled walls of a sprawling gothic manor. That's because Bell wasn't part of DreamWorks Pictures, Spielberg's movie studio, but DreamWorks Interactive, the game development studio Spielberg founded in 1995. He was the producer on the small team making Clive Barker's Undying, a first-person horror shooter made in collaboration with the author who created Hellraiser and Candyman. Last month Clive Barker's Undying celebrated its 25th anniversary and while its makers would be the first to say it wasn't a shooter that changed the direction of the games industry, they will tell you that the project was a true labour of love. They will also tell you that Clive Barker was really quite insistent that they make protagonist Patrick Galloway more fuckable. Read more

entry.title: Resident Evil Requiem review - a cathartic cross-breed of creeps and carnage
entry.summary: Resident Evil: Requiem is filled with winking reminders of previous games, so I was surprised the touchstone I kept coming back to was the one Capcom surely want me to forget: Resident Evil 6. The latter set out with bold aspirations. It took all the various reinventions the series had adopted throughout the years and spliced them into one giant hunk of Resident Evil meat, hoping it would mutate into a grisly hybrid that could channel all the styles of previous experiments. Sadly, the Resi 6 Golem also dined out on ideas from Call Of Duty and Michael Bay movies, creating more of a shallow frat bro than an ultimate life form. All these years later, Requiem feels like Capcom picking up the scalpel to take another crack at that ambitious goal. It's pulled in various test subjects, but the core elements are the skin-crawling dread of Resident Evil 7 and the karate-kicking action of Resident Evil 4 Remake. On the whole, Requiem's Golem is a stronger hybrid than Resi 6. The initial six or so hours of its lifespan are a triumph, trapping me under the weight of its oppressive horror before letting me slip free to get sweet revenge in a flurry of hyper-violence. The game starts to disintegrate into messy chunks shortly after, but those opening few hours are absolutely worth letting this prototype out of the lab. Read more
